target_customer: Individual job seekers (consumer), often free users with paid swipe tiers
problem: Applying to jobs is slow and repetitive; Sorce lets users swipe right and an AI agent fills the application on the employer's site.
business_model: Consumer subscription (one reviewer cites $15 per week for unlimited swipes); earlier a 15% recruitment commission was paused
product_category: Consumer AI job search and auto-apply app

founders.name: Oluwapelumi Dada
founders.background_notes: Built the first version, One Click Apply, per Techpoint Africa.

founders.name: Daniel Ajayi
education: MIT, CS (class of 2025 per YC page)

founders.name: David Alade
education: Northeastern University (class of 2025 per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Techpoint describes him as an iOS developer.

technical_complexity.rationale: Browser agents that fill varied employer ATS forms reliably are hard; reviewers report silent failures. Mobile apps built by a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Auto-apply is easily copied (many look-alikes); the swipe brand and audience are the main assets.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No copying or acquisition documented; competitors such as JobCopilot, LazyApply and Sprout emerged.

market_need_then: Job seekers submit many applications by hand; viral posts about the idea drew about 1.7M views in March 2024 and 1.5M in August 2024 per Techpoint.

rebrands.why: Not stated in any source found

branding.community_and_virality: Viral founder posts (1.5M to 1.7M views), Instagram over 71,000 followers, reported ranking fourth among popular US job apps in June 2025, and press debate (Daily Dot, Yahoo, Futurism) on the idea.

brand_strength.rationale: The Tinder for jobs hook and viral posts drove around 500,000 users per Techpoint; press attention was both positive and critical.

pivots.from: Paid access to jobs and a 15% commission recruitment service
pivots.to: Free platform focused on user growth
pivots.why: Per Techpoint, to grow the user base; recruitment service paused

outcome_analysis: Sorce grew from founder posts and the swipe concept to a reported 500,000 users and 20M swipes by October 2025, while joining YC in Fall 2025. Funding disclosed is small, with only Founders Inc. and angels named and no amount. Reviews are mixed on reliability and pricing, so durable retention is unproven.
notes: Round amount undisclosed (Techpoint Oct 2025); aggregators (Standout, Extruct) cite about $500K, unverified. Techpoint says the company launched in August 2024 as Swype; YC lists founded 2024 and team size 6 (Techpoint describes two founders; YC lists three). Competitor sources are dated 2025 or 2026 so competitors left empty for the Aug 2024 launch. Traction figures are self reported.
